components.text: One report, two measures: Never mix them, and name both when you quote one

notes: You may have read that a four-day week raised revenue by 35%. That misreads the UK report. It gives two numbers. For the 23 companies that reported it, revenue from the start to the end of the trial rose 1.4% on average, weighted by company size, which the report itself calls broadly the same. The 35% compares a different group of 24 companies with the same period a year earlier, so it includes ordinary business growth and is not the same comparison. Other pilots tell the same story: in Germany revenue and profit showed no significant change from the year before, and in Brazil 27.3% of companies saw revenue fall and 36.4% saw profit fall. Microsoft Japan's often-quoted 39.9% rise in sales per employee covers one month, August 2019, and Microsoft later added that it was not achieved by the four-day week alone. Our expectation for revenue is to hold it, not to grow it.
